description.narrative: Det övergripande målet för projektet som ambassaden avser stödja är att förbättra skyddet av rättigheter och välbefinnande för HBTQI+-gemenskapen i hela Kosovo
Improve the protection of rights and well being of the LGBTQI+ community across Kosovo

The overall objective of this contribution is: To improve the protection of rights and wellbeing of the LGBTIQ community across Kosovo. Moreover, this contribution will be contributing towards the following specific objectives:
With the support from the Embassy of Sweden, Center for Equality and Liberty in Kosovo will strengthen the institutional capacities, therefore. This will allow the members of the organization and the community to serve its constituencies better and in long term.
Secondly, with this support the Center will provide direct support to members of LGBTIQ persons. The support that the CEL staff offers is very diverse and covers areas of legal support, psychological and professional / academic support. This holistic approach offers a platform for LGBTIQ members to be fully integrated into Kosovo society.
Third specific objective is to work with a wider society, with the aim of raising the awareness of society on principal rights of LGBTIQ community in Kosovo, thus improving societal and institutional protection of LGBTIQ community in Kosovo.
Additionally, it will advocate with key stakeholders in Kosovo in regard to immediate needs of LGBTIQ persons, therefore ensuring policies and budgeting in Kosovo and in the region reflect the needs of this community.

Decision on contribution Support to LGBTIQ+ Community (CEL)

description.narrative:
The overall project results were achieved in 2024 as foreseen in the original plan. From them, it is worth highlighting an example of success: Diva and E., both participants in our makeup training program, took their skills to the next level by opening their own beauty studio, Queens Corner, in March 2024 just a few months after completing their training.
Despite this progress, challenges remain. A major issue in 2024 was the lack of a dedicated space for psychological sessions. Although the Municipality of Prishtina promised to provide a suitable location, this did not happen. As a result, therapists had to conduct individual sessions in their personal offices, which was sometimes inconvenient for clients. The lack of an appropriate space was even more problematic for group therapy sessions, as CEL Kosovas offices were not suitable, limiting the programs ability to offer optimal support.
The anti-gender movement continued to present challenges to the rights of marginalized communities. In response, CEL has strengthened partnerships with NGOs in Kosovo and the Balkans, focusing on advocacy, awareness campaigns, and legal actions to protect LGBTQI rights. In this context, CEL filed a lawsuit to hold individuals accountable and make clear that homophobic rhetoric will not be tolerated. Additionally, the government has yet to update the Civil Code, leaving LGBTQI individuals without full legal protections an ongoing barrier to equality.
Despite these challenges, CELs strong commitment and proactive approach provide a solid foundation for achieving our goals. Regular communication and frequent meetings between the Project Manager and Controller ensure that issues are addressed promptly.
